scope: Manual assessment of frozen final answers against predeclared final-quality-rubric.md. Findings are answer-specific, not an intelligence score.

476b696ac5fce958527117b9d3a039809a4c7490.assessment: Mostly accurate coverage with overstatements and omissions
strengths: Covers observation versus ownership, material verification, shared scheduler admission, quarantine, identity precedence, health polling and displayed progress.
938 words; ends naturally.
issues: Treats host stop contract as ensuring no zombies; supplied trait does not establish adapter correctness.
Claims ownership is only populated by spawn, overlooking handoff restoration.
Does not identify restore returning success without proof of readiness or discuss unsettled receipt ambiguity.

strengths: Two concrete examples; remaining budget, bounded retries, backoff and ambiguous payment outcomes covered.
517 words against requested 500.
issues: Says cancellation frees resources immediately; cooperative cancellation does not establish termination.
Inventory example assumes cancellation aborts reservation and releases locks without discussing committed effects or reconciliation.
Unique transaction/cart keys are presented as sufficient safe-retry assurance without durable deduplication scope.

cc76423403c02fff29fb7e338183848a49b5de1d.assessment: Does not establish safe recovery under the stated failure/race requirements
strengths: Concrete prepared/committed states, temp-file fsync, journal-before-rename ordering and crash-boundary analysis.
Recognizes cancellation after rename cannot undo committed work; 1040 words and natural ending.
issues: No operation identity, old/new content hashes or durable completion receipt; missing temp plus any existing target is treated as committed.
No explicit target-directory durability barrier before journal removal; directory assumptions are unstated.
External edit race is attributed to NFS although it also exists on local filesystems; no serialization/conflict detection.
Malformed journal may be ignored when temp is missing, erasing ambiguous state.
UI success ordering and reliable command replay are not specified.

strengths: Covers authenticated ownership, external observation, journal replay, shared admission, failure cancellation and displayed progress.
868 words; natural ending.
issues: Claims checking one controller owned field prevents multiple controllers managing the same instance; the field establishes only local custody.
Claims restore polling ensures the process is valid/matching; restore discards the readiness boolean.
Simplifies identity matching to path/alias/name alternatives, omitting explicit path precedence and directional context bounds.
Summarizes permit release on success or failure too broadly before later acknowledging failed cancellation quarantine.
Treats abstract host stop contract as proof of clean shutdown; absent adapter behavior is not verified by these files.

7f277329b191e1e02b69431b9fe38690ee253bcd.assessment: Broad coverage, imprecise identity/readiness and custody claims
strengths: Covers authenticated ownership, scheduler-by-endpoint exclusion, failed cancellation quarantine and supplied UI progress.
841 words, natural ending; explicitly marks external adapter behavior as assumptions.
issues: Simplifies identity to path/alias/name alternatives and symmetric context tolerance, omitting explicit path precedence and lower bound.
Describes restore failure as returning the original controller; the retained object is the handoff.
Does not discuss discarded readiness boolean, unsettled receipts or accepted work surviving renderer disconnect.
General conclusions that cancellation prevents leaks and UI reflects actual state overstate what visible code alone establishes.

fa166ff5edc8284a9bca13ffdab5b00f586188ce.assessment: Useful explanation, incomplete cancellation and retry guarantees
strengths: Two examples, remaining overall budget, cancellation signals, and lost-response idempotency scenario.
Explicitly says services must listen for cancellation; more precise than the baseline immediate-cleanup wording.
issues: 577 words, 77 above requested 500.
Still treats cancellation as reliably stopping work/releasing inventory locks without explaining races, committed effects or reconciliation.
No backoff/jitter or durable deduplication scope; a key alone does not prove safe retry.

07d08ca882b7aae5a746a5e0314c6dc59bd4ba31.assessment: Does not establish a safe recovery protocol; internally inconsistent replay rules
strengths: Concrete transaction ID and phases, journal-before-rename, eventual new-content checksum check, and UI update after filesystem work.
Recognizes cancellation boundary; 909 words and natural ending.
issues: Only journal fsync is specified; no durable temp contents or directory/rename durability barriers before journal deletion and UI success.
Initially treats missing/corrupt temp as aborted original-preserved state, though missing temp may follow committed rename; later replay discussion does not reconcile this rule.
Contains a false claim that a journal proves rename happened, then retracts it within the same answer.
No persisted old-content identity, conflict detection or concurrency protocol; treating missing target as failed and deleting evidence can discard ambiguous state.
Completion evidence is deleted, leaving command replay and accepted-operation reconciliation unspecified.
Cancellation after rename is suggested as a revert without requiring retained old contents or checking intervening edits.

strengths: Correctly describes retaining failed handoff, failed-cancellation quarantine, transient observation timeout, external observation and UI state distinctions.
787 words, natural ending.
issues: Identity description omits explicit path precedence and context upper bound.

Concluding robustness claims exceed visible adapter/test evidence.

0b8d1a247f1abcc6b30f568d38bea7c8f951c619.assessment: Useful broad description with a material cancellation omission
